references.title: The Automated Verification of Textual Claims (AVeriTeC) Shared Task
facts_used_in_draft: the AVeriTeC score credits a claim if and only if the verdict is correct AND the retrieved evidence meets a quality threshold
the winning team TUDA_MAI reached an AVeriTeC score of 63%
average AVeriTeC score across the 21 participating systems on Not Enough Evidence claims: 0.06; the winner scored 0.12 on Not Enough Evidence against 0.73 on Refuted

a common participant strategy was to ignore the two rarer labels; team Papelo prevented its system from predicting Not Enough Evidence and Conflicting Evidence, reporting that prompted LLMs overpredict these rarer labels
in the shared task human evaluation, on evidence annotators labeled Not Enough Evidence, systems predicted that label in 22.1% of cases and Refuted in 60.3%
the organisers removed fact-checking articles from the knowledge store after finding they had leaked into the evidence set for some claims
